Package io.webagent4j.policy.network

package io.webagent4j.policy.network
Network-destination governance: INetworkPolicy decides whether WebAgent4J may make a network request to a given destination, evaluated strictly before the request is sent.

This is independent of, and complementary to, action authorization ( io.webagent4j.action.policy, webagent4j-action) and crawl-scope policy ( ICrawlScopePolicy in webagent4j-crawler-api, "should this URL be followed as part of the crawl graph"). All configured gates must pass independently - a crawl-scope policy allowing a host does not imply a network policy allows requesting whatever address that host currently resolves to, and vice versa.

Honest limitations (see docs/governed-execution.md for the full discussion): this package prevents a request before it is sent whenever the pipeline evaluates this policy first, which is true for HttpCrawler (every redirect hop) and for a governed browser NAVIGATE action or crawl (the initial navigation). A browser's own internal redirect handling cannot be intercepted mid-flight, so a redirect that lands somewhere the policy would have denied is only detectable after that navigation already happened - reported accordingly, never misrepresented as prevented. DNS pre-resolution checks the addresses a hostname resolves to at evaluation time; it is not transport-level pinning and does not by itself defend against DNS rebinding between check and connect. This package makes no claim to be a complete SSRF firewall.

  • Class
    Description
    INetworkAddressAuthority
    Capability an INetworkPolicy may additionally implement to expose the exact, freshly resolved and individually-authorized IP address set for one destination, so a transport can bind its actual connection to that same set instead of performing its own, independent resolution that could silently observe a different result between the check and the connection - the DNS rebinding / time-of-check-to-time-of-use gap this interface exists to close.
    INetworkAddressResolver
    Resolves a hostname to the addresses it currently maps to.
    INetworkPolicy
    Authorizes one network request before it is sent (or, when the requesting backend cannot be intercepted mid-flight - see NetworkCheckPhase.POST_REQUEST - checks it immediately after).
    NetworkAddressCategory
    Classification of one resolved InetAddress against well-known special-use IPv4 and IPv6 address ranges.
    NetworkAddressClassifier
    Classifies one InetAddress into a NetworkAddressCategory using only java.net - no third-party CIDR library.
    NetworkCheckPhase
    When, relative to the actual network request, a NetworkPolicyContext is being evaluated.
    NetworkDestination
    A safe, canonicalized description of a network destination - the only view of a requested URL an INetworkPolicy ever sees.
    NetworkPolicies
    Builds standard, declarative INetworkPolicy implementations from allow-lists and deny-by-category rules, so most callers never need to implement INetworkPolicy themselves.
    NetworkPolicies.Builder
    Mutable builder for a declarative INetworkPolicy.
    NetworkPolicies.NetworkResolutionFailedException
    Thrown when network-address resolution itself fails during evaluation - caught by the governed pipeline exactly like any other RuntimeException thrown from IExecutionPolicy.evaluate(C), so it fails closed identically to a DENY.
    NetworkPolicyContext
    Immutable, structured description of one network request about to be authorized.
    NetworkPolicyReasons
    Stable reason codes used by the built-in NetworkPolicies implementation.
    NetworkRequestKind
    What kind of network request a NetworkPolicyContext is describing.
    VerifiedNetworkAddresses
    The exact IP addresses a transport is authorized to connect to for one destination, in resolution order, alongside the logical hostname it must still present for the Host header, TLS SNI, and certificate hostname verification - the physical address is never a substitute for the logical hostname in any of those three places.
